newsitem.title: CANADA: Conciliator works on Inco labor dispute.
newsitem.headline: Conciliator works on Inco labor dispute.

text.p: Talks to resolve a labor dispute at Inco Ltd's Manitoba facility stalled on Tuesday as a government conciliator tried to foster understanding between the two sides.
The conciliator met with separately with union and company negotiators twice on Tuesday but neither side reported progress.
"We are just going to wait and see what the process unfolds," said Inco spokesman Dan McSweeney.
About 1,400 United Steelworkers were locked out of the plant on Sunday after they rejected an Inco contract offer.
Inco produces about 100 million pounds of nickel a year from the Thompson area in northern Manitoba, or 20 percent of Inco's total output.

Laboour negotiations broke down over shift scheduling and wages. While union negotiators said they were willing to work with the conciliator, they said they would rather meet directly with Inco representatives.
"We've got to bargain this thing," Bob Desjarlais, president of local 6166, said in an interview. "Bargaining by edict is just unacceptable."
Inco said it has not tried to ship products out of the facility since the lock out began. The plant produces a wide range of electrolytic nickel products for the melting and plating industries.
Analysts estimate that Thompson accounts for about 5.6 percent of the world's nickel supply.
Inco has vowed to continue supplying its customers by using products from its other facilities or buying on the world market if necessary.
